question: A cylinder is inscribed in a sphere. The radius of the sphere is (5)/(6) times the height of the cylinder. What is the ratio of the volume of the cylinder to the volume of the sphere?
solution:
**Given:**

A cylinder is inscribed in a sphere

The radius of the sphere is (5)/(6) times the height of the cylinder.

**Formula used:**

Volume of cylinder = πr²h

Volume of sphere = 4/3 πr³

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/409b6d6aad0b24a1730ea66b02d3a60e37cb0ac065b90d5cb2ae6e8abaf8b8c0.png] 

The radius of the sphere is (5)/(6) times the height of the cylinder.

The radius of sphere = 5

The height of cylinder = 6

Now,

According to the figure

⇒ (Radius of cylinder)² = (5)² – (3)²

⇒ (Radius of cylinder)2 = (25 – 9)

⇒ (Radius of cylinder)2 = 16

⇒ Radius of cylinder = 4

Now,

⇒ Volume of cylinder/Volume of sphere = πr2h/4/3 πr³ 

⇒ [π × (4)² × 6]/[4/3 × π × (5)³]

⇒ (16 × 6)/(4/3 × 125)

⇒ 96/(500/3)

⇒ 288/500

⇒ 72/125

⇒ 72 : 125

**∴ The required ratio is 72 : 125**
